summary.description: Total Organic Carbon (TOC) refers to any carbon-containing organic compound dissolved in water and is used as a general indicator of water quality. It includes a wide variety of compounds.
emission_sources: Any man-made or natural process releasing organic compounds to water
environmental_impact: Elevated TOC levels reduce oxygen in water, fostering anaerobic bacteria growth
Disruption of aquatic ecosystems and natural water body functions
Potential indirect human health impacts depending on the specific chemicals involved

top_sdg_impacts.SDG6_Clean_Water_and_Sanitation: TOC is a key indicator of water quality. High levels can compromise safe and clean water, making it harder to ensure access to sustainable water management and sanitation.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG14_Life_Below_Water: High TOC levels reduce oxygen in aquatic environments, promoting anaerobic conditions and threatening aquatic biodiversity and ecosystem stability.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG12_Responsible_Consumption_and_Produc: TOC pollution often stems from improper waste management and industrial discharges, highlighting the need for more sustainable production and disposal practices.
